passages.text: The tame birds frequenting the roofs of our houses, defend their fledglings. Others build their nests, and hatch their young, in the tops of mountains and in the precipices of valleys, and the holes and tops of trees, and keep off the intruder. And if not able to do this, they fly circling round them in agony of affection, calling out in their own note, and save their offspring in whatever manner they are able.
passages.note: a parent's protective love and helplessness
